The cost of disconnected operations

Fund operations shouldn’t depend on constant reconciliation.

When fundraising, investor onboarding, governance, and reporting sit across separate systems, keeping them aligned becomes another operational responsibility.

The cost is more than administrative overhead. Decisions, capital activity, and supporting documents become harder to reconcile into a clear picture of how the firm operates.

For managers: less reconstruction

Each close, reporting cycle, or diligence request can send the team back across systems to assemble the same information. That effort grows with every vehicle and investor relationship.

For investors: a clearer basis for conviction

A compelling strategy starts the conversation. Consistent records of decisions, capital activity, and reported results help investors assess what sits behind it.

The opportunity is to connect the workflow and the evidence, rather than reconstruct the relationship between them later.

One operating foundation, from first commitments to ongoing reporting.

Fish Network is designed to connect the core workflows around an investment firm. Investor relationships, vehicle activity, decisions, and reports remain connected to the people and documents behind them.

One connected operating foundation

Fish Protocol is the underlying blockchain architecture. It is designed to make selected activity traceable and changes to recorded history detectable, while keeping confidential documents subject to appropriate access controls.

The first deployment model

Put the platform to work through a Fish School.

A Fish School is the investment group and operating workspace through which participants use Fish Network. It connects the manager or organizer, participating investors, and the workflows around their vehicle.

For a new launch, the conversation starts with structure and operating requirements. For an existing firm, it starts with the workflows you want to connect, the providers you need to retain, and where a supported deployment could fit.

The reputation layer

Give the track record more context.

Performance matters. So does understanding the role a manager or contributor played in producing it.

Fish Points is the proposed reputation mechanism for connecting recorded participation and contributions to the people behind them. Alongside the underlying investment records, it is intended to make that history easier to examine over time.

  1. Record a relevant contribution, decision, or capital event.

  2. Connect it to the participant and available supporting evidence.

  3. Keep related activity and subsequent outcomes connected over time.

  4. Give investors and counterparties a clearer basis for reviewing the participant’s role.

Participation records are not audited performance. Fish Points does not certify every claim, establish investment skill, or guarantee an outcome.

Explore Fish Points

Built beyond the first vehicle

A new vehicle shouldn’t mean starting the operating history again.

The Neofund thesis explores how investment firms can carry relevant relationships, processes, and records forward as they grow. The legal vehicle may change. The organization’s operating knowledge should not have to be rebuilt around it.

Fish Schools are the starting point for deployment. Neofund describes the longer-term organizational thesis, not a requirement for using the platform.
